Petya paints each cell of a $22\times 22$ board black or white so that the cells of each colour form a polygon. Then Vasya cuts the board into two-cell dominoes. Petya wants as many two-coloured dominoes as possible to result, and Vasya wants as few as possible. What largest number of two-coloured dominoes can Petya guarantee, however Vasya acts?

(Recall that the boundary of a polygon is a closed broken line without self-intersections.)

Several zeros were inserted between the two eights of the number $88$. Prove that one can always append several more digits on the left, at the beginning of the new number, so as to obtain a number that is a perfect cube.

A piece of cheese of mass $1$ kg was cut into $n\geqslant 4$ pieces of mass less than $600$ g. It turned out that they cannot be divided into two heaps so that the mass of each heap is at least $400$ g but at most $600$ g (a heap may consist of one or several pieces). Prove that there are three pieces such that the total mass of any two of them is more than $600$ g.

Let $O$ be the centre of the circumcircle of an acute triangle $ABC$. A point $D$ is marked on the side $BC$. The circles circumscribed about the triangles $BOD$ and $COD$ meet the segments $AB$ and $AC$ again at the points $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Prove that a triangle can be formed from the segments $BX$, $XY$ and $YC$.

Call a subset $A$ of the plane line-like if for some line $\ell$ of the same plane there is a bijection $f\colon\ell\to A$ such that for any two points $X$, $Y$ on the line $\ell$ the length of the segment $XY$ differs from the length of the segment $f(X)f(Y)$ by at most $1$. Is it true that every line-like subset of the plane lies between some two parallel lines?

A magician and his assistant are going to perform the following trick. The assistant blindfolds the magician, invites a random spectator from the audience onto the stage and asks him to write a sequence of zeros and ones of length $2^{2025}$. Then the assistant correctly tells the magician the position and the value of some one term of the sequence. The magician's task is to guess $2025$ other terms of the sequence (i.e. to name their positions and values). Prove that they can agree in advance so that the trick succeeds.

Is it possible to place at the vertices and at the midpoints of the edges of a regular octahedron one natural number from $1$ to $18$ each, so that all the numbers are distinct and at each vertex stands the number equal to the sum of the four numbers standing at the midpoints of the edges issuing from this vertex? (See the figure.)

Let $I$ be the centre of the circle inscribed in a triangle $ABC$. On the sides $AC$ and $AB$ the points $K$ and $L$ respectively are taken such that the line $IK$ is perpendicular to $CI$, and $KL$ is parallel to $BI$. Prove that the triangle $LKI$ is isosceles.

Petya and Vasya play the following game. First each of them writes a one on his own board. Then in turn (Petya begins) each replaces his own number by multiplying it either by $2$ or by $3$, and after each move the numbers written on the boards must be distinct. Let $a$ be the number of natural divisors of Petya's number after his $100$-th move, and $b$ the number of natural divisors of Vasya's number after his $100$-th move. As the result of the game Petya receives $|a-b|$ sweet wrappers. For what largest natural $n$ can Petya act so as to be guaranteed to receive at least $n$ wrappers regardless of Vasya's actions?

A hotel has $a>1$ floors, with $b$ single rooms on each floor. $ab$ mathematicians arrived at a mathematical congress. It turned out that each mathematician likes exactly one room on each floor. Prove that the number of ways to accommodate all the mathematicians in the hotel so that each likes his room is even.

Nadya has thought of a polynomial $P(x)$ with real coefficients. In one move Maxim may name any polynomial $Q(x)$ with real coefficients, and in reply Nadya must tell Maxim the following two facts:

• whether the maximum value of $P+Q$ is attained, and if so, what it is equal to;

• whether the minimum value of $P+Q$ is attained, and if so, what it is equal to.

Maxim wants to make several such moves in succession and then name a number $t$ such that $|P(2026)-t|<10^{-100}$. Prove that Maxim can act so as to be guaranteed to achieve what he wants. (Maxim himself decides when to stop asking questions.)

The base of a convex quadrilateral pyramid $SABCD$ is a quadrilateral $ABCD$ whose diagonals are perpendicular and no two of whose sides are equal. It is known that the inscribed spheres of the tetrahedra $SABC$ and $SACD$ touch. Prove that the inscribed spheres of the tetrahedra $SABD$ and $SBCD$ touch.

In each cell of an infinite squared plane one real number is written so that the sums of the numbers in all groups of cells forming a "staircase" (see the figure) are the same. Can there be at least $89$ distinct numbers among those written?

Real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ are such that
$$a+\operatorname{arctg}b>c+\operatorname{arctg}d,\qquad b+\operatorname{arctg}a>d+\operatorname{arctg}c.$$
Prove that $a+b>c+d$.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ the altitudes $AD$, $BE$ and $CF$ meet at the point $H$. Three circles with centres at the points $D$, $E$, $F$ passing through $H$ meet the lines $BC$, $CA$ and $AB$ respectively at six distinct points. Prove that these six points can be divided into two triples so that for the two triangles formed by these triples of points there is a circle touching all six lines containing the sides of these triangles.

In a class consisting of at least $5$ pupils (girls and boys) a test was held. It is known that during the test every pair of pupils communicated, and exactly one of the pupils in this pair helped the other. As a result it turned out that for each pupil, among those whom he helped there were equally many girls and boys. How many pupils could there be in the class?

Call a natural number $N>1$ good if there are natural numbers $a_1, \ldots, a_N$ such that the greatest common divisors of all possible pairs of them form $N(N-1)/2$ consecutive natural numbers. Is there a good natural number greater than $10^{100}$?
